To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the maximum likelihood criterion is the best method to estimate diffusion model parameters when data are uncontaminated; (b) the Kolmogorovan–Smirnov criterion is the best choice when data contain contaminants; (c) the chi-square method should be avoided, especially in the case of small numbers of trials; (d) the performance of fast-dm methods is comparable to that of the EZ approach, but not as precise as that of the Bayesian implementation; (e)

(1) for uncontaminated response time distributions, maximum likelihood estimation is superior to other optimization criteria, but (2) in the presence of outliers, the Kolmogoroff–Smirnov criterion is more robust.
maximum likelihood is the best choice for most situations, Kolmogrov–Smirnov should be used when fast responses are present in the data, and chi-square is not a reliable choice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what is needed for reliable parameter estimation, which is an important question in any field of science.
the development of methods for robust parameter recovery in diffusion modeling and the evaluation of these methods in a series of simulation experiments.
the question of how many trials are necessary for reliable parameter estimation in diffusion models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no “one size fits all” solution.
the choice of the optimization criterion depends on the type of data.
there are no clear-cut recommendations for a single method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
maximum likelihood is the method of choice for parameter estimation in binary decision tasks.
the number of trials required for reliable parameter estimation depends on the model complexity and on the optimization criteria used.

for models with more than 4 parameters (i.e., 2 drift rates and 2 boundary separation values), at least 100 trials are required to obtain reliable parameter estimations, whereas models with only 3 or fewer parameters can already be estimated reliably from as few as 25 trials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of optimization criteria and the model complexity should be carefully matched to the experimental conditions.
for most cases, the fast-dm method based on maximum likelihood is a reliable method to estimate parameters of a diffusion model.

the choice of optimization method should be guided by the expected quality of the data, and the modeler should be aware of the fact that the optimization method can have a strong effect on the parameter estimates.
